summary_paragraph: A woman with a long history of recurrent abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting was admitted after an episode of hematemesis. Despite extensive prior evaluations, no definitive cause such as chronic pancreatitis or vasculitis was confirmed. She was managed with IV fluids, pain control, and antiemetics. A GI consult attributed the bleeding to a likely Mallory-Weiss tear from retching. Methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine were discontinued due to lack of confirmed rheumatologic disease. A parotid biopsy was scheduled to confirm Sjogren’s syndrome. Amitriptyline was tapered due to concerns about gut motility. The patient elected early discharge, tolerating liquids, and was given Emend as a rescue anti-nausea medication. A long-term plan involving primary care, chronic pain management, and psychiatric follow-up was recommended.
